title: 3 years living with a heat pump - stats and my main take-away
summary: A UK owner reports three years of metered heat pump data in a Victorian terrace: COP rising to 3.5, about £200 a year cheaper than an efficient gas boiler on a smart tariff, and an 18-25 year payback.

assertions.quote: for every unit of electricity that we've used we've got three and a half units of heat out
this is not a particularly well insulated home
what we're doing now is we're trickling in heat all the time

verdicts.note: For variable-speed air-source units, 'set it and forget it' beats setbacks: homes without setbacks saved $10-$100 more a year; flow temperature (hydronic) is not studied.

Morning and evening setbacks made the heat pumps call higher stages of resistance heat to recover, so the authors recommend a constant setpoint or gradual setbacks; this supports steady operation for ducted units but says nothing about flow temperature.

assertions.quote: at a price cap tariff our heat pump would have had a similar cost to run as a very efficient gas boiler
octopus's smart tariffs tend to be much cheaper than the price cap when running a heat pump
solar panels generating free P power to power our heat pump and therefore free Heat
reduced our heating emissions by almost 70%
a simple calculation would suggest around 18 to 25 years

verdicts.note: Even over 16 years, unsubsidized NPV is positive for only 55% (minimum), 41% (medium) and 21% (high-efficiency) of homes, far from a few-year payback for all.
Only 21% of US single-family houses without heat pumps would benefit economically over a 15-year life from replacing their heater with one.

In RMI's gas retrofits, heat pumps either raise energy costs (Chicago, Providence) or save too little to recover the extra capital (Houston, Oakland), so for most gas homes they never pay back at 2018 prices.
Edwards finds 19% of households would face higher bills and 28% no clear change, so a heat pump cannot pay for itself through bills for nearly half of homes.
Payback is 5-6 years only when the existing heating or cooling system has failed; as a pure retrofit it typically exceeds 10 years, so 'a few years' holds only at replacement time.

For UK households replacing gas boilers, operating costs are higher, not lower, on a standard tariff, leaving a net private cost of about £4,121 over 20 years, so there is no payback from bill savings.

The report says lower heat pump operating costs offset the higher capital cost within a few years (citing Kaufman 2019 and Goody 2014), but its own model shows this depends on region and fails in many Edmonton cases.

assertions.quote: I might have asked for some bigger radiators or for some more radiators
this would usually come with the Grant from the boilet upgrade scheme
an average heat pump installation is now around
